findings.reason: the node that adds the accessor must either migrate pulse_mint._served_entries onto it or state why pulse_mint keeps its own raw time-base read, otherwise the design ships the duplicate it claims to have removed.
findings.text: pulse_mint._served_entries resolves each SignalRule's rule.source_group and rule.source_array itself and reads the raw channel through imas_ambix/data/eddb.py read_channel to obtain that channel's own time base; this is the identical rule-to-source resolution that imas_ambix/data/virtual_zarr.py:134-135 already owns inside VirtualZarrView.__getitem__, and it is the exact need the §6 node jtmm-observation-time-alignment adds an untransformed accessor to serve (imas_ambix/data/cocos_convention.py:800-817 is the only site the plan migrates). The plan's sentence "That leaves one owner of rule-to-channel resolution, adds one accessor to the view and retires nothing" is a census of one, not of the type, so the new accessor ships with a same-shaped bypass still live beside it.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the two new public surfaces (§6 read_signal_map_observation, imas_ambix/data/cocos_convention.py:759, and the EQDB request/record types added to imas_ambix/data/eddb_remote.py) hide a kernel, a store dispatch and a framing change behind small interfaces, and extend RemoteEddbExtractor/eddb.py rather than spawning a second engine or store.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the plan asserts it leaves "one owner of rule-to-channel resolution" (§6) but its census counts only its own site; imas_ambix/data/pulse_mint.py:206 resolves rule.source_group/rule.source_array and reads the raw channel through read_channel, a second site un-migrated onto the untransformed accessor it is adding.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; every implementable section accounts for its own surface in its text (the pin table retires three public definitions and their re-export in imas_ambix/gs/artifact_resolution.py and imas_ambix/spine_bench/machine_artifact_arm.py and adds one; read_signal_map_observation retires one and adds one; the EQDB request and record types, the eddb grid writer, the JT-60SA frozen shot set and the two scalar record fields each state they retire nothing and why nothing can be), so no section adds to a family without naming its retirement, merge, or the reason none is possible.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan names and the review verified the existing machinery each proposed mechanism extends (score_convention/format_sign_report and the private _integrated_current kernel in imas_ambix/data/cocos_convention.py, judge_geometry in imas_ambix/eval/efit_referee.py, ForwardOperator.vacuum_prediction and assemble_pf_currents in imas_ambix/gs/operator.py:578/582, read_geometry_table's probe_angle_source branch at imas_ambix/data/description_reader.py:253-257, the eddb read_channel/write_channel store, and the artifact_resolution pin constants), and cites what it searches rather than proposing a parallel subsystem.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the wrappers the plan would add are extensions of an existing owner with the extension stated, not parallel layers: read_signal_map_observation replaces read_catalogue_observation (one retired, one added), read_geometry_table gains a probe_angle_source branch rather than a fifth probe-angle supplier, and the grid writer is folded behind helpers extracted from write_channel so the token and overwrite contract has one implementation.
